C
An infinite sum, or series, is the process of adding together a sequence of terms that has no end. While some infinite series diverge to infinity (D), many converge to a finite value.

B
A convergent series is one where the sequence of partial sums approaches a specific, finite limit (its sum). A divergent series is one where the partial sums do not approach a finite limit; they may grow infinitely large or oscillate.

B
The convergence of a series depends on its partial sums approaching a limit. The distance between two real numbers, such as a partial sum and its limit, is fundamentally measured by the absolute value of their difference.

B
The 2-adic distance between two numbers is small if their difference is divisible by a high power of 2.

C
In the 2-adic metric, the "size" of 2^n gets smaller as n increases, causing the series to converge. The standard geometric series formula a/(1-r) applies, giving the sum 1/(1-2) = -1.
